title: 2.2 Fix stuck note on release off the keyboard
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`PanelPointer`).

**What to implement:** `PanelPointer` only clears `held_key`/calls `PanelNoteOff` inside the keyboard band (`e.y >= kKeyY && e.y < kKeyY + 56`). A press on a key followed by an upward drag + release lands in a different branch, so the note never stops and `held_key` stays set — notes accumulate. Hoist the release handler to the top of `PanelPointer`, before any geometry test: `if (e.kind == kRelease && p->held_key >= 0) { PanelNoteOff(freq); p->held_key = -1; }`. Delete the now-redundant release branch inside the keyboard band.

**Done conditions:** A press then off-band release produces exactly one note-off (no stuck/accumulated notes). Regression test added to `tests/test_panel.cc`. `ctest` green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Envelope playhead does not animate
description:
**Target files:** spike/panel.cc (PanelDraw), tests/test_panel.cc.

**What to implement:** The playhead is time-based (NowMs), but the env plot only redraws when dirty (note-on/off, param change), so the dot froze between events. Invalidate the env plot every frame while a note is held or releasing: `if (p->note_on || EnvLevel(NowMs(), *p) > 0.001f) MarkDirty(p, 2);` in PanelDraw. The curve is unchanged, so the column-update skip keeps this cheap.

**Done conditions:** The env plot redraws every frame while a note is active (draw count increments in steady state); ctest green.
close_reason: PanelDraw invalidates the env plot each frame while note_on or releasing (EnvLevel > 0.001); the playhead now traces. Added steady-state animation check. ctest 12/12, cm33 65576 B (25.02%), host smoke clean.

title: MIDI CC reaches the display
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`SyncFromEngine`, `PanelDraw`, `PanelPointer`), `tests/test_panel.cc`.

**What to implement:** CC wrote the engine directly, but `SyncFromEngine` was only called from the drag paths, so the display froze. Make `SyncFromEngine` change-detecting (compare six params, `MarkDirty` on change) and call it each frame from `PanelDraw`; drop the manual sync/mark from the drag paths. Align the panel's cached defaults with the engine's `g_params` defaults.

**Done conditions:** An `EngineSetParam` with no pointer event redraws the affected plot; ctest green.
close_reason: SyncFromEngine is change-detecting and polled each frame from PanelDraw; drag paths no longer sync/mark manually. Panel defaults aligned to engine. Added no-pointer-event redraw test. ctest 12/12.

title: Readout: two-line format with units
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`ReadoutText`, `DrawReadout`, `MarkDirty`).

**What to implement:** The envelope readout (up to 320 px) overflowed the 230 px clear band. Split filter and envelope readouts into two lines (matching the mockup's `reads` layout) while keeping units: filter `1.00kHz` / `RES 50%`; envelope `A 0ms  D 0ms` / `S 70%  R 0ms`. Clear and damage the full two-line band (2*font.h + 2).

**Done conditions:** Each line fits within the band (no leftward spill); golden hash updated; ctest green.
close_reason: Filter + envelope readouts split into two lines (units kept); clear + damage the 2-line band. Golden hash -> 0xC1DBB623. ctest 12/12.

title: 2.4 Make ScopeRing race-free + TSan coverage
description:
**Target files:** `controller/scope_ring.h`, `controller/scope_ring.cc`, `tests/test_scope_ring.cc` (new), `CMakeLists.txt`, `test-tsan.sh`.

**What to implement:** `buf_` is plain `float`, written by the audio thread and read by the UI thread — a genuine data race (TSan: `scope_ring.cc:6`). Change `float buf_[kCapacity]` to `std::atomic<float> buf_[kCapacity]` and use `memory_order_relaxed` `store`/`load` (lowers to plain loads/stores on ARM; makes the race well-defined). Add a `test_scope_ring` target with a two-thread write/read harness, and add it to the `test-tsan.sh` build list.

**Done conditions:** `test-tsan.sh` reports no data race on the ring; `test_scope_ring` passes under normal and TSan builds. `ctest` green.
close_reason: Fix: buf_ -> std::atomic<float> (relaxed); test_scope_ring added + wired into test-tsan.sh; ctest 12/12. TSan runtime blocked in container (setarch -R not permitted) - run test-tsan.sh on host.

title: 2.3 Fix phantom key 0 left of the keyboard
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`PanelPointer`).

**What to implement:** `const int idx = (e.x - kTitleX) / kKeyW;` truncates toward zero, so `e.x = 4` yields `(4-16)/76 == -12/76 == 0` and the `idx >= 0` guard never fires — any touch in x in [0,16) plays C. Guard on the raw coordinate: `if (e.x >= kTitleX && idx < 13)`.

**Done conditions:** Touches at x < kTitleX do not trigger a note-on. Regression test added. `ctest` green.
close_reason: Closed

title: 2.1 Fix envelope handle overlay trails above the plot
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`DrawEnvPlot`).

**What to implement:** Handle rects `ha{e.xA-13, e.T-13, 26, 26}` and `hd{e.xD-13, e.yS-13, 26, 26}` have y == -1 when the handle is at the plot top (T == 12, or sustain -> 1). `Cursor()` draws through `FillRect` (clipped to the whole frame), so the top bar is written one row above the plot; `EraseOverlayRect` clamps `y0 = max(0, r.y)` so that row can never be erased. Clamp the handle rect y at construction: `ha{e.xA-13, std::max(0, e.T-13), 26, 26}` and `hd{e.xD-13, std::max(0, e.yS-13), 26, 26}`.

**Done conditions:** Dragging the attack/decay handle leaves no lit row above the envelope plot. Regression test added. Golden hash updated (handles drop 1 row). `ctest` green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Activate fb.clip in the plot draw
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`PlotOsc`/`PlotFilter`/`PlotEnv`/`PlotOut`, `DrawEnvPlot`).

**What to implement:** `ColumnUpdate`/`EraseOverlayRect` honored `fb.clip` but nothing narrowed it, so the 3.2 hardening was inert. Save/set/restore `fb.clip` to the plot rect around each plot draw (readout drawn after restore), then drop the `std::max(0, ...)` handle clamps — the clip now confines overlays to the plot.

**Done conditions:** Handles clipped to the plot without the manual clamp; golden hash updated; ctest green.
close_reason: fb.clip save/set/restore to the plot rect in the 4 hooks; dropped std::max(0,...) handle clamps (clip now confines overlays). ctest 12/12.

title: 2.5 Implement ColumnUpdate skip + trace reset
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`ColumnUpdate`, `PanelDraw`).

**What to implement:** `ColumnUpdate` documents a skip ("columns whose span matches the trace are skipped") but the loop has none — every curve column is erased+redrawn on every draw. Add `if (old_on && new_on && tr.y0[x] == lo[x] && tr.y1[x] == hi[x]) continue;`. This cannot land alone: `DrawChrome` wipes the frame with `FillRect(kBg)` and does not reset `traces`, so the skip would leave unchanged columns blank over a wiped background. Reset the current buffer's traces in the full-render path before drawing the plots: `for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) std::memset(&p->traces[i][b], 0xFF, sizeof(TraceState));`. Both halves together.

**Done conditions:** Unchanged columns are not rewritten (verify via a probe/harness), the curve never vanishes across a mode-switch full redraw, and `ctest` green (pixels identical — no hash change).
close_reason: Closed

title: 3.4 Unify panel/backend buffer index
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.{h,cc}`, `host/sdl_backend.{h,cc}`, `target/zephyr/cm33/src/main.cc`, `target/zephyr/cm33/src/glcdc_backend.{h,cc}`.

**What to implement:** `Panel::fb_index` and the backends' own toggle (SDL `current`, GLCDC `back_`) advance independently and must agree; if `PanelDraw` is ever called twice per present or `Present()` early-returns, they desync and every subsequent trace lookup hits the wrong buffer. Pass the buffer index into `PanelDraw` (or derive it from `fb.px`), removing `Panel::fb_index` so there is a single source of truth.

**Done conditions:** One buffer index, no independent toggles. `ctest` green, host smoke clean, cm33 `west build` green.
close_reason: PanelDraw now takes the buffer index from the backend (single source of truth, no independent toggle). SDL BackIndex() + GLCDC back_ pass it; test passes explicit indices. ctest 12/12, host smoke clean, cm33 65148 B (24.85%).

description: Fixes and hardening from the 2026-09-10 independent code review of spike/, controller/scope_ring.*, target/zephyr/cm33/, host/main.cc. Confirmed defects (2.1-2.5), latent risks (3.1-3.6), and perf items (4.1-4.3).

title: 3.2 Clamp scope y + honor fb.clip in hot paths
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`DrawScopePlot`, `DrawCyclePlot`, `DrawSpectrumPlot`, `ColumnUpdate`, `EraseOverlayRect`).

**What to implement:** The three scope paths compute `y = mid - lround(buf[x] * amp)`; if the IPC tap ever delivers samples beyond +/-1, `y` leaves the plot then the framebuffer, and `tr.y0[x] = (uint8_t)y` silently wraps. Clamp `y` to `[0, h-1]` in the three paths. Also make `ColumnUpdate`/`EraseOverlayRect` honor `fb.clip` (they currently write `fb.px[...]` with no bounds test).

**Done conditions:** Out-of-range samples clamp without out-of-bounds writes (probe harness). `ctest` green (no change for valid samples).
close_reason: Closed

title: 3.1 Track the readout band in the damage rect
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`MarkDirty`).

**What to implement:** `MarkDirty` adds only `plots[idx].rect` (y in [142,374)), but the plot hook also calls `DrawReadout`, which writes at `kReadoutY = 390` (y in [390,410)) — entirely outside the damage rect. This works only because damage is a gate, never a clip. Add a second damage rect for the readout band so damage stays complete if it ever becomes a clip or DMA source: `Rect{kPx0[idx] + kPlotDX, kReadoutY, kReadoutX - kPlotDX, kPrimaryFont.h}`.

**Done conditions:** The damage set covers both the plot and its readout band. `ctest` green (no pixel change).
close_reason: Closed

title: 3.5 Add cache maintenance before GLCDC flip
description:
**Target files:** `target/zephyr/cm33/src/glcdc_backend.cc`, `target/zephyr/cm33/prj.conf`.

**What to implement:** `CPU_CORTEX_M85` selects `CPU_HAS_DCACHE` and `CONFIG_DCACHE` defaults y, but the display driver does zero cache maintenance, so the two SDRAM framebuffers can be scanned out stale. Add `sys_cache_data_flush_range()` over the just-written back buffer before `display_write` (or mark the SDRAM framebuffers non-cacheable via MPU). Build-verified only; hardware behavior is a bring-up item.

**Done conditions:** cm33 builds with the flush in place; the change is flagged "confirm on bring-up" and NOT closed as HW-verified.
close_reason: Resolved: cm33 runs on Cortex-M33 (no D-cache; .config has CPU_CORTEX_M33, no CPU_HAS_DCACHE). No cache flush needed; finding documented in Present().

title: 3.3 Add size-coupling static_asserts + BDF BBX check
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.h` (or `spike/panel.cc`), `tools/bdf_to_c.py`.

**What to implement:** No assert ties the silent size couplings: `TraceState::y0/y1[230] >= kPlotW`, `Panel::col_lo/col_hi[256] >= kPlotW`, `DrawScopePlot::buf[256] >= kPlotW`, `TraceState` element `uint8_t` requires `kPlotH <= 255`, and `kEmpty == 0xFF` must be unreachable as a real y. Add `static_assert(kPlotW <= 230)`, `static_assert(kPlotH <= 255)`, `static_assert(kPlotW <= 256)`. In `bdf_to_c.py`, verify every glyph's BBX matches the font-bounding-box cell (zero offsets) so a future font swap fails loudly.

**Done conditions:** Asserts compile; `bdf_to_c.py --check` still exits 0 on Terminus; a mismatched font fails the check.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bake Zephyr Python build deps into the Dockerfile
description:
## Context

The Zephyr target build needs Python packages absent from the Docker image.
They were installed ad-hoc into the container's system site-packages with
`pip3 install -r zephyr/scripts/requirements-base.txt`, which is wiped on every
image rebuild. The SDK, Zephyr tree, and `west` are already baked or live in
the persistent /workspace — the Python deps are the one thing that is not.

## Problem

On a fresh container, `west build` fails at CMake configure with
"Missing jsonschema dependency" (zephyr_module.cmake:73). The deps must be
re-installed by hand after every restart.

## Fix

Bake the Zephyr base build requirements into the Dockerfile pip layer
(alongside `west`). Install the packages from
`zephyr/scripts/requirements-base.txt` that the build actually imports
(jsonschema, PyYAML, pyelftools, pykwalify, packaging, intelhex, semver,
anytree, …), skipping the test/compliance extras
(requirements-build-test.txt / requirements-compliance.txt) that are not needed
to build.

## Expected

A fresh container runs `west build -b ek_ra8d2/r7ka8d2kflcac/cm85 …` with no
`pip3 install` step — the deps are present in the image.

## Evidence

First build failed at configure: `CMake Error … Missing jsonschema dependency`
(zephyr_module.cmake:73). `requirements-base.txt` is the "required to build"
set; `requirements.txt` pulls the test/compliance extras that are unnecessary.
close_reason: Baked the Zephyr build-imported Python deps (jsonschema, pykwalify, PyYAML, pyelftools, packaging, intelhex, anytree, semver) into the Dockerfile pip layer. Verification (fresh-image west build) pending image rebuild.

title: Cut control-rate powf/tanf coefficient recompute (dirtiness tracking)
description:
## Context

`bench --breakdown` (5 s, desktop) shows the full voice at ~9.9 ns/sample, of
which "env+coeff+overhead" is 5.28 ns (53%) — more than the SVF filter itself
(2.65 ns). Oscillator 1.96 ns; filter/osc ratio 1.35x.

## Problem

`update_filter_coeffs()` (engine/engine.cpp) runs unconditionally every
control step (16 samples). It maps normalized cutoff -> Hz via `powf` and
computes the TPT SVF `g` via `tanf`, even when nothing changed (fixed cutoff,
sustain, filter_env=0). This violates the digest's own "dirtiness tracking"
principle: coefficients are recomputed that did not need recomputing.

## Fix

1. Replace the exponential cutoff->Hz mapping (`powf`) with a lookup table or
   cheap polynomial — control-rate accuracy does not need `powf`.
2. Add a dirtiness flag: recompute SVF coefficients only when the effective
   cutoff/resonance changes (parameter setters, or envelope crossing a
   threshold), not every control step.

## Expected

Full voice ~10 -> ~7 ns/sample on desktop. Proportionally larger win on the
M85, where `powf`/`tanf` are software-emulated (no FPU).

## Evidence

`bench --breakdown`: osc 1.96, filter 2.65, env+coeff+ovh 5.28, full 9.90 ns/sample.
close_reason: Dirtiness tracking in UpdateFilterCoeffs: skip the pow/tan recompute when env_cutoff+Q are unchanged; sentinel in StartNote. Bench -38% coeff, -23% full voice.

title: 4.3 Add touch move events + atomic g_touch (board-gated)
description:
**Target files:** `target/zephyr/cm33/src/glcdc_backend.cc`.

**What to implement:** `PollTouch` maps only pressed/released — no `kMove` — so dragging works only via repeated press events, which re-runs `HitTestEnv` per event (a drag can jump between handles). Also `g_touch` is a non-atomic struct written from the input callback thread and read from the main loop, and `INPUT_EV_SYN` is not handled, so x/y can be read torn or mid-batch. Make `g_touch` atomic, batch on `INPUT_EV_SYN`, and emit `kMove` on ABS_X/ABS_Y. FT5336 event semantics (continuous move events, coordinates) must be confirmed on hardware.

**Done conditions:** Blocked — needs an EK-RA8D2 board to verify the FT5336 event stream.
notes: Board-gated: no EK-RA8D2 board in this environment; FT5336 event stream (move/SYN) must be verified on hardware.

Either exercise the merge/collapse path in `test_damage`, or collapse `Damage` to a 4-bit mask and delete the unreachable machinery.

**Done conditions:** The merge path is covered by a test, or the machinery is removed and the class simplified. `ctest` green; flash delta recorded.

Options: decimate to 2048 bins, run the FFT on a slower cadence than the redraw, or move it to the M85 (FPU + cache). This is blocked on a frame-time measurement on the target to settle whether it is even worth it.

title: 3.6 Document display_write flip semantics
description:
**Target files:** `target/zephyr/cm33/src/glcdc_backend.cc` (comment).

**What to implement:** Verified against `zephyr/drivers/display/display_renesas_ra.c`: with `CONFIG_RENESAS_RA_GLCDC_FB_NUM=0`, a full-frame `display_write` takes the `l_pend_buf = buf` path and calls `R_GLCDC_BufferChange` (hardware flip), then blocks on the line-detect semaphore — it does NOT memcpy. The copy path only exists for partial writes and only when `FB_NUM >= 1`. Record these verified semantics (and the FB_NUM=0 full-frame-only requirement) in the backend comment so the design is documented against the driver source.

**Done conditions:** Comment accurately reflects the driver source; cm33 `west build` green.
close_reason: Documented verified display_write semantics: FB_NUM=0 full-frame path -> R_GLCDC_BufferChange (hardware flip, not memcpy); memcpy only for partial writes (rejected with FB_NUM=0).
